2027-02-01.title: New Places, Same God
2027-02-01.verse: So Abram moved his tents and went to live by the oaks of Mamre in Hebron, and he built an altar to the Lord there.
2027-02-01.observation: Abraham has had some family drama. He finally decides it is best to separate from his family and go to a new area. The first thing he does is to dedicate this new place to the Lord. This is such a great reminder to us all. Even when circumstances cause our surroundings to change, it does not change the Lord. He is always faithful and always close. No matter what changes, we can always celebrate that He never does.
2027-02-01.application: Where do you need to be reminded that the Lord has not changed?
2027-02-01.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for Your continual faithfulness.

2027-02-02.title: The Lord is the Blessing
2027-02-02.verse: But Abram replied to the king of Sodom, “I raise my hand to the Lord, the Most High God, Creator of heaven and earth, and vow that I will take nothing belonging to you, not even a thread or the strap of a sandal. That way you can never say, ‘It is I who made Abram rich.’
2027-02-02.observation: Abraham was living his life in a way that everyone knew all he had came from the Lord. He continues it in this passage by saying he will not receive a reward from these people so they cannot take credit for Abraham’s blessing. While it is fine to receive gifts from others, it is always important to remember where the true blessings come from. All good gifts come from the Lord.
2027-02-02.application: See everything in life as a gift from the Lord.
2027-02-02.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for always providing for all our true needs.

2027-02-03.title: The Lord Knows Us
2027-02-03.verse: After these things the Lord’s message came to Abram in a vision: “Fear not, Abram! I am your shield and the one who will reward you in great abundance.
2027-02-03.observation: At this point in the story of the life of Abraham, it may seem as though he has no more worries or fears. God has blessed him and all seems to be going well. However, the Lord truly knows us. Therefore, despite the look of blessing, the Lord knew Abraham needed to be reminded not to be afraid. We can hide our true feelings from others, and sometimes that is not a bad thing. However, the Lord truly knows us and will meet our true needs. Don’t ever be afraid to be honest with the Lord. He already knows.
2027-02-03.application: Tell the Lord about it all.
2027-02-03.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for truly knowing us.

2027-02-04.title: Don’t Try to Help God
2027-02-04.verse: So Sarai said to Abram, “Since the Lord has prevented me from having children, please sleep with my servant. Perhaps I can have a family by her.” Abram did what Sarai told him.
2027-02-04.observation: Sarai realizes the problem with God’s plan. It’s great that He wants to give them a family. However, she likely feels she has not lived up to her end of the deal by not being able to have children. Therefore, she is trying to fix her inability by offering an alternative. The problem with this is that doing so would require them to act without integrity. Often it can be difficult to know where our responsibility ends and God’s miracles begin. God wants us to do our best, but He also works in all things for His will. It is not a good idea to stop trying and just say the Lord will do it. It is also not good to work like it only depends on you. A possible balance is to do the best you can, but never act outside of God’s moral law. Anything that requires more than what you can give is in the hands of God. Don’t try to “help” God by breaking His law.
2027-02-04.application: Do the best you can, but stay within the boundaries of integrity. Trust the Lord to do the rest.
2027-02-04.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for having a plan for us and working it out in spite of us.

2027-02-05.title: The Promise and the Condition
2027-02-05.verse: When Abram was ninety-nine years old, the Lord appeared to him and said, “I am the Sovereign God. Walk before me and be blameless. Then I will confirm my covenant between me and you, and I will give you a multitude of descendants.
2027-02-05.observation: The LORD tells Abraham that his job is to be faithful and pure while God’s job is everything that is impossible. God starts with telling Abraham who He is so Abraham knows that God is able to hold up His end of the covenant. God is not asking for Abraham to do anything he cannot already do. The point is to be faithful. Many parents do this with their children. They tell them they can earn an allowance by cleaning their room. The chore is well within their ability. The goal is not because the parents need their help. The goal is so they have a part in the process. This is how God works. He is not interested in spoiled children. He doesn’t need our “help.” He gives us the opportunity to partner with Him for our benefit.
2027-02-05.application: Do your part and watch God do His.
2027-02-05.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for leading us with the hand of a faithful Father.

2027-02-06.title: Is Anything Too Hard for the Lord?
2027-02-06.verse: The Lord said to Abraham, “Why did Sarah laugh and say, ‘Will I really have a child when I am old?’ Is anything impossible for the Lord? I will return to you when the season comes round again and Sarah will have a son.” Then Sarah lied, saying, “I did not laugh,” because she was afraid. But the Lord said, “No! You did laugh.
2027-02-06.observation: The easy answer to the question of whether anything is too hard for God is no. The hard answer is, “If God can do anything, why do we doubt Him?” This is because it is easy to declare and hard to walk out. The great thing about God is He gets us. Therefore, He does not refuse to bless us just because we do not understand how He does it. Our job is not to figure God out. Our job is to trust Him, do the best we can, and watch Him do the rest.
2027-02-06.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for constantly doing more than we can imagine.

2027-02-07.title: The Amazing Mercy of God
2027-02-07.verse: When Lot hesitated, the men grabbed his hand and the hands of his wife and two daughters because the Lord had compassion on them. They led them away and placed them outside the city.
2027-02-07.observation: The city had been condemned by the justice of God. He was no longer willing to allow the city to be so evil without justice. Lot deserved the same judgment because he seemingly refused to leave. However, as an act of amazing mercy, the angel of the Lord physically took him outside the city! Even then, he allowed Lot to negotiate the rescue by allowing him to decide what city he ran to. Think of how much “power” over the situation he thought he had. God’s grace allowed him to actually have some of what he asked. This is such a great picture of us. We have been saved from destruction by the gracious hand of God. However, we still act like we can dictate the terms of our rescue. May we never be so arrogant. Instead, may we be thankful and follow the Lord wherever He determines we should go.
2027-02-07.application: Take a moment to realize how much amazing mercy the Lord has shown us through His salvation.

2027-02-08.title: The Lord Blesses Us Through Rejection
2027-02-08.verse: Then in the dream God replied to him, “Yes, I know that you have done this with a clear conscience. That is why I have kept you from sinning against me and why I did not allow you to touch her.
2027-02-08.observation: Have you ever thought something was a good idea, but you just could not get it to work out? In this passage, it appears Abimelech decided it would be a good idea to take Sarah and did not see any reason not to move forward. The Lord stopped him. He did not know it at the time, but God’s goodness was shown to him through what he was unable to do. While we never want to think of the negative things in our lives being allowed by the hand of God, the truth is God is sovereign over all things. God is not the author of evil, but He allows evil to have its time due to the free will granted to us all. However, God is also not limited by evil. He can still work through difficult circumstances. God’s “no” turned into the best “yes” Abimelech could have hoped for in life. What about you? Even if it is uncomfortable, think about a time in your life when things did not work out. Is it possible that “no” saved you from something worse?
2027-02-08.application: How has God helped you by saying no?
2027-02-08.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for leading us even when we do not know what’s best.

2027-02-09.title: The Lord Keeps His Word
2027-02-09.verse: The Lord visited Sarah just as he had said he would and did for Sarah what he had promised.
2027-02-09.observation: The greatest news we can ever hear is that the Lord keeps His promises. The Lord told Abraham and Sarah they would have a child. This was impossible. Abraham was 100 and Sarah was 90. However, nothing is impossible with the Lord. What is even more amazing is they had not been perfect since that promise was given. They tried to make it happen on their own. None of this forfeited God’s ability to do something amazing. We cannot stop God’s promises once they are given. God is faithful.
2027-02-09.application: Is there a promise from God’s Word that you need to hold to today?
2027-02-09.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for being faithful.

2027-02-10.title: Trust God in the Hard Days
2027-02-10.verse: Early in the morning Abraham got up and saddled his donkey. He took two of his young servants with him, along with his son Isaac. When he had cut the wood for the burnt offering, he started out for the place God had spoken to him about.
2027-02-10.observation: I cannot imagine how difficult it must have been to get up in the morning, knowing what God had asked Abraham to do. It took an amazing amount of trust to do this. Abraham knew God had promised to make him a great nation. He knew this would not be possible if Isaac was no more. Therefore, he knew either God would intervene or bring Isaac back to life. This is an amazing amount of trust. This is what God asks of us. We are not required to figure out what the Lord is doing. We are required to trust that He is trustworthy. We follow and trust the Lord to do the right thing, the right way, and trust that all things will work out for good.
2027-02-10.application: Where do you need to keep following God, even though you don’t understand?
2027-02-10.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for leading us in the right direction.

2027-02-11.title: Pay Your Way
2027-02-11.verse: So Abraham agreed to Ephron’s price and weighed out for him the price that Ephron had quoted in the hearing of the sons of Heth—400 pieces of silver, according to the standard measurement at the time.
2027-02-11.observation: Abraham insisted on paying for the property so it could be his without any misunderstandings or need for kindness in the future. This is important for many reasons. Many friends grow distant over time. With that distance comes difficulty in maintaining sincere promises made during closeness. Business deals can go well for a while, only to sour when a “better deal” comes along. The idea is to not allow something important to go with a mere word. Pay your way. Pay the value of something. Create binding promises for your sake and theirs.
2027-02-11.application: Is there a promise you made in the past that you need to remember to honor today?
2027-02-11.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for not merely telling us of Your love, but showing us every day.

2027-02-12.title: The Lord Guides Our Path
2027-02-12.verse: He prayed, “O Lord, God of my master Abraham, guide me today. Be faithful to my master Abraham.
2027-02-12.observation: The servant of Abraham knew that he needed God’s help to accomplish his mission. Instead of trying to do it alone, he asked for the Lord’s help and the Lord guided his steps. We have to remember that the servant did not pray for help and then did nothing else. He did all he could do, but trusted the Lord to go with him and guide his steps. This is a helpful lesson for us all. We should always ask the Lord for guidance, but that does not mean we should sit and think He will bring the result to us. We apply ourselves and do all we can. Then, we trust the Lord to guide our steps, open the right doors, and do all the things we cannot do ourselves.
2027-02-12.application: Where do you need to pray for guidance and then take the next right step?
2027-02-12.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for always guiding us along the way.

2027-02-13.title: Be Careful Not to Overlook What You Have
2027-02-13.verse: Then Jacob gave Esau some bread and lentil stew; Esau ate and drank, then got up and went out. So Esau despised his birthright.
2027-02-13.observation: Scholars have wondered what would cause a firstborn son to give away his rights as the firstborn. As the firstborn son, you were the second line of leadership, you received the majority share of your father’s inheritance, and you were the one in charge of keeping the family safe after your father could no longer lead. It was an honored position. However, Esau did not seem to care for it to the point he was easily willing to give it away. How many times do we take for granted the wonderful things the Lord has placed in our lives? Some of these gifts could be the home we live in, the friends we have, or our family. These true gifts are only noticed once they are gone. Be careful not to treat as common the things that are the true blessings of life.
2027-02-13.application: Take time today to look around and be thankful for the consistent blessings in your life.
2027-02-13.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for the million little miracles we take for granted every day.

2027-02-14.title: Obedience Pays Off
2027-02-14.verse: The Lord appeared to Isaac and said, “Do not go down to Egypt; settle down in the land that I will point out to you. Stay in this land. Then I will be with you and will bless you, for I will give all these lands to you and to your descendants, and I will fulfill the solemn promise I made to your father Abraham. I will multiply your descendants so they will be as numerous as the stars in the sky, and I will give them all these lands. All the nations of the earth will pronounce blessings on one another using the name of your descendants. All this will come to pass because Abraham obeyed me and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.
2027-02-14.observation: Isaac was not like his father. However, God still had a plan for his life and God was going to continue the legacy that began with his father, Abraham. When the famine struck the land, it would have likely been the most sensible idea to go to Egypt like his father had done. The Lord told him to stay faithful where he was. While Isaac did not do it perfectly, he stayed and the Lord blessed him. This is a great lesson for our lives. Most of the time, God will not tell us to move on to greener pastures, but to grow where we have been planted. Even if we do not do it perfectly, the Lord will guide our steps. While we are not always supposed to stay put in hard times, we often stay where God has placed us because He is doing more than we can currently see.
2027-02-14.application: Is God calling you to stay and grow where you have been planted in this season?
2027-02-14.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for being able to make a miracle out of all our messes.

2027-02-16.title: Trust the Word Over the Feeling
2027-02-16.verse: So Jacob went over to his father Isaac, who felt him and said, “The voice is Jacob’s, but the hands are Esau’s.
2027-02-16.observation: When it comes to knowing God, it is important to realize that God’s Word is central to knowing Him. This must be stated because it is easy to become addicted to good feelings and ignore the truth of God’s Word. There are many reasons why this happens, and it is important to remember that emotions are not bad. However, they make terrible leaders. Therefore, we enjoy emotions, but live by God’s Word. If not, we can fall into the same trap as Isaac. He thought he was doing a good thing only to find out that he damaged himself and the next generation.
2027-02-16.application: Be sure to have proper boundaries between your emotions and the truth you live by.
2027-02-16.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for teaching us how to live by the Truth of Your Word. That Truth brings life, peace, and a lasting joy.

2027-02-17.title: Set Up Ways to Remember
2027-02-17.verse: Then this stone that I have set up as a sacred stone will be the house of God, and I will surely give you back a tenth of everything you give me.
2027-02-17.observation: Jacob had an encounter with God. Afterward, he set up a way to remember this experience. Now, whenever he passed by again, he would remember what the Lord had done. He could also share his testimony with others. Then, when they passed by, they would remember the Lord’s faithfulness. We still need to do this today. We do not need to create stone pillars or memorials, but we need to write down the wonders of the Lord in our lives. Not only that, but we need to tell others what the Lord has done. This way, we can remember God’s faithfulness. Remembering His faithfulness gives us assurance that He will continue to be faithful.
2027-02-17.application: Start a journal and write down some of the great things the Lord has done. Over time, you will be thankful for the reminders.
2027-02-17.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for giving us so many moments to be thankful for.

2027-02-18.title: Turn Your Perspective to Praise
2027-02-18.verse: She became pregnant again and had another son. She said, “This time I will praise the Lord.” That is why she named him Judah. Then she stopped having children.
2027-02-18.observation: The story of Leah and Rachel is one of the saddest stories in the Old Testament. These two daughters seemed to be so busy competing with one another that they were unable to enjoy growing a great family. While they competed, they were giving birth to the patriarchs of the twelve tribes of Israel. This shows in Leah naming her first sons after the difficulty she was experiencing. When having Judah, she finally begins to see that God is blessing her with children. How many times do we struggle, fight, and complain our way through life? While doing so, God is slowly giving us more than we realize and doing things we should be thankful for. What would happen if we stopped looking at what others have to determine our worth, and instead looked at what God has already done in us?
2027-02-18.application: How can you shift your perspective to see your life as a blessing?
2027-02-18.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for blessing us in more ways than we realize.

2027-02-19.title: What Does Your Presence Do to Others?
2027-02-19.verse: But Laban said to him, “If I have found favor in your sight, please stay here, for I have learned by divination that the Lord has blessed me on account of you.
2027-02-19.observation: Have you ever heard the phrase that says some people make the environment better simply by leaving? This is not something anyone wants to be known for, but is it true? On the other hand, some people make an environment better simply because they are present. Many times these people bring an element of fun, an element of encouragement, or maybe they are a hard worker. One time, when my wife and I were moving, she told me a relative was coming to help. Instantly I knew it was going to be okay, because this relative was one of the kindest and hardest workers I had ever met. What about you? What do people think when they hear you are on the way? Are they secretly unhappy to hear it or do they look forward to your company? Do they know you will make things better because you bring the integrity of a man or woman of God? Does your relationship with God rub off on others?
2027-02-19.application: How can you bring your relationship with God with you into your life today?
2027-02-19.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for walking with us through every moment of every day.

2027-02-20.title: God is Helping You More Than You Know
2027-02-20.verse: There he said to them, “I can tell that your father’s attitude toward me has changed, but the God of my father has been with me. You know that I’ve worked for your father as hard as I could, but your father has humiliated me and changed my wages ten times. But God has not permitted him to do me any harm.
2027-02-20.observation: When my girls were little, they loved feeling like they could drive. They would get in my lap and I would drive through a parking lot. They would have their hands on the steering wheel and they could steer around. Not only that, but they would be so excited. They thought they were driving just the way they watched me do every day. What they did not realize was that I had my hand on the bottom of the steering wheel and I operated the gas and brake. The whole time they thought they were doing all the driving, but they really had much more help than they could see. If God somehow truly opened our eyes, we would be surprised to realize that God helps us much more than we realize. We may have our hands on the “steering wheel” of our life, but He does too. He also operates the gas and brake. He’s protecting us. He’s stopping bad things and bringing good things. If we saw all He was doing, we would worry less and trust Him more.
2027-02-20.application: How would you live your day if you truly understood the Lord is in control?
2027-02-20.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for kindly leading us through every single day.

2027-02-21.title: The Lord Visits Us In Our Dark Times
2027-02-21.verse: So Jacob was left alone. Then a man wrestled with him until daybreak.
2027-02-21.observation: This text is intriguing. Most scholars believe this is a Christophany. This means a time when Jesus (the visible image of the invisible God) showed up in the Old Testament. If this is the case, the ramifications can speak to us even today. Jacob was in big trouble. He did not know what the next morning would bring. He was concerned that his family would be killed. He had prepared as best he could and was waiting for the dawn. In our darkest moments, God visits us. Sometimes, we struggle with Him. We do not always realize it is the Lord bringing us His presence and comfort. However, once we have “done business” with the Lord, we are ready to face the world. The Lord comes to comfort us and to change our lives.
2027-02-21.application: If you are going through a “dark night of the soul,” look around. The Lord is there with you.
2027-02-21.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for never leaving us. In our darkest moments, You are there.

2027-02-22.title: Sufficient Is the Trouble of the Day
2027-02-22.verse: But Esau ran to meet him, embraced him, hugged his neck, and kissed him. Then they both wept.
2027-02-22.observation: When Jesus is speaking about worry in Matthew 06, He ends by saying to not worry about tomorrow. There’s enough trouble in today to keep you busy. He is not saying that we should allow ourselves to worry today. He is simply saying stay focused on what is in front of you. Jacob was right to prepare in case of trouble, but he should not have allowed worry to consume him. When Jacob met with his brother, he was not attacked. He was embraced. I heard a quote one time that said 90% of the things we worry about will never happen. Of the 10% that does happen, 8% are beyond our control. In no scenario would anyone think it was a good bet to do something that only had a 2% chance of success. However, we do it all the time. So, let the words of Jesus echo in our hearts today. Prepare for tomorrow, but live in today. It has enough to keep us busy.
2027-02-22.application: How can you best organize your day to prepare for tomorrow, but focus on today?
2027-02-22.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for already being in tomorrow and making a way we don’t even know we need.

2027-02-23.title: Deal With Injustice Righteously
2027-02-23.verse: Then Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “You have brought ruin on me by making me a foul odor among the inhabitants of the land—among the Canaanites and the Perizzites. I am few in number; they will join forces against me and attack me, and both I and my family will be destroyed!
2027-02-23.observation: The sons of Jacob were placed in a difficult position. Their sister had been assaulted and justice needed to be done. During the time, there was no local police force. If someone did harm to you, it was your job to dispense justice. Many look at the words of Jacob as being uncaring toward his daughter or self-centered. It appears as though he is thinking only of his personal interests. However, when you think more broadly of the context, you can see his dilemma. Jacob desires justice for his daughter, but also needs to do so in a way that does not do more harm than good. He realizes that justice can become injustice when it goes too far. Justice should have come to the man who did the deed, not the entire community. We must be careful to remember the same. Justice is a good thing and the Bible speaks a lot about the purpose of justice in our world. However, justice must meet the crime. We must also be careful not to allow others to get wrapped up in our rage.
2027-02-23.application: Do you have a pattern of taking out injustice on the innocent? How can you course correct today?
2027-02-23.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for always dealing with us in a just and righteous way.

2027-02-24.title: Set the Tone
2027-02-24.verse: So Jacob told his household and all who were with him, “Get rid of the foreign gods you have among you. Purify yourselves and change your clothes. Let us go up at once to Bethel. Then I will make an altar there to God, who responded to me in my time of distress and has been with me wherever I went.
2027-02-24.observation: Jacob set the tone for his family by saying they were to remove all the idols from their houses. They were going to serve the Lord as one family. This is sad in a way, because it seems to indicate that this had not already happened. Likely, there were those in his family who either did not worship the LORD or were polytheistic. However, Jacob set the tone by saying all that was over. They were going to worship the LORD and he was going to go first and make sure it happened. In our family and friend groups, someone has to go first and set the tone. Everyone around you needs someone who is willing to go first and set the tone for following Jesus. This does not mean we become militant or try to force people to follow Jesus. However, we should live our faith out in such a way that inspires others to follow the LORD, too.
2027-02-24.application: Does everyone around you know that you follow Jesus? Do you follow Jesus in such a way that it is encouraging to others?
2027-02-24.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for being worth following.

2027-02-25.title: The Reality of Life
2027-02-25.verse: What follows is the account of Esau (also known as Edom).
2027-02-25.observation: There is an uncomfortable reality that no one wants to talk about. When we read through this chapter, many people confess to skipping over many of the names. The reason for this is because these names mean nothing to us. They appear to be little more than a means to continue the family line. They are another link in the chain that eventually gets to another prominent figure. There are many more “links” than prominent figures. The uncomfortable reality is that you and I will more than likely be a “link” and not a “prominent” figure. However, we need to realize that God knows where we fit. Every one of these people were necessary for the “chain” to continue. If one of these people is missing, if they are not making sure the chain continues, if they do not continue teaching the next generation the importance of continuing the chain, the entire chain could be broken. If you ever feel like you do not matter and you do not have a purpose, zoom out and see that you are vital to the chain. Without you, the chain will be broken. Don’t just live for yourself, live for those who have come before you and those who will come after you. Do not let the chain of God’s faithfulness in your family be broken.
2027-02-25.application: How can you be faithful in honoring your “place in the chain” today?
2027-02-25.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for letting us be part of Your generational plan.

2027-02-26.title: Doing the Right Things The Wrong Way
2027-02-26.verse: Joseph had a dream, and when he told his brothers about it they hated him even more.
2027-02-26.observation: God had given Joseph a dream. If you have read the rest of the story, you know that dream happened. Therefore, we see it was indeed a dream from the Lord. The dream said that Joseph would one day lead his family. This would have been unheard of during their time. The oldest brother was in charge of the family after the father died. Being in charge of the family did not simply mean getting your way, it meant having the responsibility of caring for and protecting the family, too. Therefore, to say this to his brothers would have been foolish as well as a disrespect to the oldest brother. Joseph had a dream from the Lord, but he unintentionally weaponized it against his family. We can unintentionally use what the Lord is doing to cause strife in our family. When the Lord blesses you, it is not a time to make sure everyone knows it. A testimony is not a chance to brag or belittle. It is a time to celebrate the goodness of God. We have to be careful that we do not use what the Lord is doing as a weapon against someone else.
2027-02-26.application: Be careful to always give the Lord glory for all He does for you.
2027-02-26.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for teaching us wisdom and how to honor You in front of others.

2027-02-27.title: The Importance of Self-Awareness
2027-02-27.verse: Judah recognized them and said, “She is more upright than I am, because I wouldn’t give her to Shelah my son.” He was not physically intimate with her again.
2027-02-27.observation: This chapter covers something that was very important for the time. It was called the levirate law. Because there was no social safety net to protect and care for the most vulnerable people in the community, the levirate law was established. This law meant that someone would step in and care for a widow by providing them with a child. This gave the woman status within the extended family unit and provided a possible future with a continued family of her own. There were many benefits to this law, and it was designed to care for widows who would become destitute without help. Judah should have done this, but chose to care more about himself and what he considered important rather than Tamar. When Judah realized what had happened, he had enough self-awareness to acknowledge his sin and not condemn Tamar. In life, we will not always get it right. The only thing worse is to continue to defend a sinful position because we are unwilling to measure ourselves the same way we measure others. When we realize we are not perfect, we open the door to see from the point of view of others and increase our compassion.
2027-02-27.application: How can you increase your self-awareness today?
2027-02-27.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for growing us in many different ways.

2027-02-28.title: The Lord Is With You In Dark Places
2027-02-28.verse: The warden did not concern himself with anything that was in Joseph’s care because the Lord was with him and whatever he was doing the Lord was making successful.
2027-02-28.observation: Joseph had received a previous promise from God. It would seem as though his life went from bad to worse ever since. However, when we read the story of Joseph, there are little hints that God is guiding his life. He goes to a slave owner’s house and slowly becomes the administrator of the home. He is placed in prison and slowly becomes the administrator of the prisoners. Joseph doesn’t know it yet, but all of this is preparing him to administrate the entire nation. We do not always understand why God allows the dark seasons of life, but we can confidently understand that He does not waste them. Is it possible that the dark season you are in is preparing you for the next opportunity just around the corner?
2027-02-28.application: How would it change your perspective to realize the Lord is with you in every dark season of life?
2027-02-28.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for walking with us through every dark place.
